Starting from identity edge and rational orthogonal gauges g(a)=I,g(b)=J=[[0,-1],[1,0]], the constructed transformedL differs from G L G^-1 and sends the transported parallel section(1,0,0,1)to(2,0,0,2).
findings.limits: Valid unitary rational2x2countermodel with positiveunitweight and one edge. Separate gauge_fixing.rs517–627 uses correctly oriented incidence and D*WD and passes the independentcontrol; finding is specific to legacy laplacian.rs.

findings.title: Perturbation bound trusts nonnegative weights without checking them
findings.statement: A four-cycle with alternating weights+1,-1has all weighted diagonal degrees0and a nonzero Hermitian Laplacian. Its certificate reports operator_norm_bound0for epsilon2. Changing every unittransportI to-I gives nonzero Hermitian delta with absolute row sum4, contradicting that numerical bound.
findings.limits: The control violates the documented nonnegative-weight convention, which compute/certificate do not enforce. For admitted nonnegativeweights and Hermitian perturbations, the written Weyl-Gershgorin bound is appropriate. The unperturbed gap is supplied, not independently measured.

findings.title: Face flatness and arbitrary loop products do not certify pure gauge or homology pairing
findings.statement: is_flat returns true on every face-free graph regardless of cycle holonomy. A two-cycle graph with noncommuting unipotent transports has a commutator loop with zero H1class but nonidentity transport; cycle_homology_pairing returns that raw matrix despite its H1pairing label.
findings.limits: Localfaceflatness is valid narrowerpredicate. Newer gauge_fixing::holonomy_verdict explicitly distinguishes FlatNontrivial from GaugeTrivial and computes fundamentalgeneratorresiduals. The qualified Bianchi function is not refuted.

findings.title: Nested built-in Gaussian scalar is not a field and rank hides inversion refusal
findings.statement: GaussianRational<T> implements ExactScalar for every ExactScalar T, including GaussianRational<BigRational>. The nonzero outerelement(inner i,inner1)has norm i²+1=0and refuses inversion; rank of its1x1matrix silently returns0because exact_inv errors are discarded.
findings.limits: Ordinary QandQ(i)overQare unaffected. Nested built-in instantiation shows the trait bound is insufficient for advertised field elimination; a domain restriction or propagated error is needed.

findings.title: Several operation-limit parameters are not enforced on the mathematical work
findings.statement: curvature_commutator names its limits argument _limits and uses unbounded matmul. Path holonomy uses try_identity/matmul without max_dimension or contraction limits; matmul_with_limits itself checks only result rows/columns, admitting arbitrarily wide inner dimension under a small dimension limit. Indexed incidence and D*WD have genuine work checks, but flat_cyclic_gauge_classes allocates faces*z without checked multiplication or its own operation cap; trivial connection allocates identities before dimension admission.
findings.limits: Checked integer products and allocation failure handling remain useful. This is a declared budget boundary gap, not evidence that ordinary small calculations are wrong.

findings.title: Capacity-wrapper tests are not mathematical owner tests
findings.statement: The appended count/capacity BoundaryRecord tests in connection,curvature,holonomy,laplacian and matrix exercise only unrelated integer admission inequalities. Their mutation-accounting labels do not provide controls for inversion,curvature,holonomy,Laplacian or elimination. Gauge_fixing likewise has only capacity-wrapper inline tests; signed_transport and gauge_quotient append literal Ok/Err tag tests despite their substantive runtime checks. Modular.rs also appends only literal Ok/Err tests; catalog appends only a count/capacity test. These do not establish modular identities or catalog realization.
findings.limits: These wrapper tests are meaningful for the wrappers themselves. Separate integrations/historical campaigns were not run; graph cochain and functional-orbit inline tests are substantive and are distinguished.

findings.title: Root-of-unity helper falsely reports field insufficiency for large exponents
findings.statement: FusionScalar::root_of_unity multiplies k by w/n with checked i64 multiplication before reducing modulo w. For GaussianRat,w4,n1,k=i64MAX, it returns None and the public wrapper reports FieldTooSmall although the requested first root is exactly1.
findings.limits: Safe refusal rather than false acceptance/panic. Reducing k modulo n before multiplication avoids the spurious refusal; ordinary small exponents and genuine field exclusions are unaffected.

findings.title: Galois wording conflates changed pivotal signs with fixed associator data
findings.statement: The dimension prose says the same F data admit Galois-conjugate dimension vectors, and the Z2 test calls rational signs +1 and -1 Galois conjugate. Field automorphisms fix rational1. For the catalog Fibonacci F00=phi^-1, conjugating d=phi to (1-sqrt5)/2 while keeping F fixed gives d²F00²=(7-3sqrt5)/2, not1; true Galois conjugation also changes F. The checker correctly rejects this inconsistent combination.
findings.limits: Documentation/mathematical characterization defect, not false acceptance by dimension consistency checks. Alternate pivotal characters can produce rational sign changes, but are not Galois automorphisms.

findings.title: RepS3 example does not test the multiplicity-free admission boundary
findings.statement: The test described as a multiplicity obstruction uses RepS3, whose std tensor std is 1+sgn+std and has no coefficient above1. FSymbols::trivial rejects it because it is not pointed, so this test cannot demonstrate rejection of a genuine multiplicity2 fusion rule. The actual coefficient gate exists and is separate.
findings.limits: Test adequacy/label issue only. Independent RepA4 table gives a genuine multiplicity2 positive ring for a future gate control; no retained Rust tests executed.

findings.title: Unverified modular data can return the wrong Frobenius-Schur indicator
findings.statement: ModularData::from_ribbon permits degenerate ribbon categories and does not verify modularity. Its frobenius_schur_indicator method nevertheless uses the modular Bantay formula and accepts any result in {-1,0,1} without invoking verify or checking duality. For symmetric pointed Vec(C3), F=R=1 and dimensions1 pass the ribbon equations; S is all ones and singular, yet the method returns1 for both nonselfdual simple labels, whose second indicator is0. The separate verified constructor correctly refuses the singular S.
findings.limits: Admission/API boundary defect rather than a counterexample on verified modular input. from_ribbon openly documents its weaker status, but the invariant method does not enforce its additional prerequisite. Ground-state and central-charge labels likewise need the modular interpretation premise; no physical observation is established.
